To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miR- 143 and miR145 were originally reported to be tumor suppressors in colorectal cancer.
miR-145/143 are highly expressed in fibroblasts but not in colon epithelial cells and that the expression of miR-145 is up-regulated in colon cancer cells.
miR-145/143 are not tumor suppressors, but rather are important regulators of mesenchymal cell differentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
miRNA biology and the importance of cell type-restricted miRNA expression patterns in the context of cancer biology.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miRNAs have cell type-restricted patterns of expression, and it is critical to consider this information in the design and interpretation of miRNA research studies.
miRNAs are not tumor suppressors in all cell types and the cell type in which a miRNA is expressed should be considered when determining its function.
cell-type localization of a given miRNA must be determined before its role in a particular disease process can be fully understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell type-specific miRNA expression should be considered when studying the role of miRNAs in cancer.
